metadata.purpose: Redo (Plain register) of the locked claude-basics/what-is-claude-basics source: answers what actually changes your results with Claude in the first week. Lands the carry-out that a blank chat and an empty project behave the same — Claude only sharpens once you feed it the documents you'd otherwise keep re-explaining.

beats.narration_text: You wonder if Claude just isn't smart enough for your work. It's not that — it's not fed enough. Here's what actually changes your results in the first week.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive framing, hesitates on 'smart', corrects to 'fed', lands the real question

props.text:
Is Claude just
not smart
enough for my work?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. Replaces source's Teardown computational-skepticism cold open. Liam speaks the naive framing, notes the correction, then reads the final corrected question over the typing animation.

beats.narration_text: Two people use Claude for a week. One's answers stay generic no matter what they ask. The other's get sharper by day three — same exact model.

shot.new_visual_element: Two people, same model, diverging output

production_viz.label: Same model, different results
production_viz.mechanic: Two simple person-dot icons on the left, both feeding into one identical 'MODEL' box in the centre. Two output lines diverge on the right: one flat labelled 'still generic' (crimson), one climbing labelled 'sharper by day 3' (teal).

beats.narration_text: The obvious read: the first person just isn't asking good questions — or needs a smarter model. Reasonable guess. It's also wrong.

shot.new_visual_element: NOT SMART ENOUGH? -> SMARTER MODEL, sold as reasonable

production_viz.label: The obvious guess
production_viz.mechanic: Large 'NOT SMART ENOUGH?' in bold INK. Below, an arrow to a bigger box labelled 'SMARTER MODEL'. Sell this as reasonable — no crimson break yet, this is the wrong guess, not the falsification.

beats.narration_text: Even the sharpest model can't know what you never told it. By default, every new chat starts blank — no files, no history, no memory of last week.

shot.new_visual_element: SMARTER MODEL struck through; repeated BLANK CHAT boxes across weeks

production_viz.label: No index of you to miss
production_viz.mechanic: 'SMARTER MODEL' from S02 reappears, struck through in crimson. Beneath it, three identical 'BLANK CHAT' boxes labelled Week 1 / Week 2 / Week 3 in a row, all the same. Crimson strike is the beat's only accent.

beats.narration_text: The second person works in a project instead: real documents already loaded, a thread that keeps its history. Picture the three documents you keep re-explaining at work — that's the one to hold onto.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — three stacked documents beside a PROJECT frame with a history thread

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — three documents
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Three small rectangle 'document' icons stacked on the left in INK. A teal-outlined 'PROJECT' frame on the right with a thin curling line inside it labelled 'history'. Label beneath the documents: 'the three you keep re-explaining'. THIS EXACT THREE-DOCUMENT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S05.

beats.narration_text: So tonight: take those three documents — the ones you re-explain most — and put them in one project. That's the whole move. Feed it what it needs, and the output stops being generic.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same three documents, sliding into the project frame

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — load them tonight
production_viz.mechanic: THE S04 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical — three stacked documents, teal PROJECT frame. Now the three documents animate sliding INTO the frame. Label beneath: 'tonight: load these three.' Teal accent on the frame border as the documents land inside it.

beats.narration_text: When the project is genuinely loaded — the real documents, the actual history — the model stops defaulting to generic and starts answering like it knows your work.

shot.new_visual_element: LOADED PROJECT, teal check, specific output

production_viz.label: Loaded — specific
production_viz.mechanic: A PROJECT frame filled with three document icons and a teal checkmark. An arrow labelled 'genuinely loaded' points to an output box reading 'SPECIFIC' in teal bold. Teal is the beat's accent.

beats.narration_text: An empty project doesn't count. One you create but never load behaves exactly like a blank chat — the label changed, the context didn't. Extra files you never open don't help either.

shot.new_visual_element: Mirrors S06: EMPTY PROJECT, crimson X, still generic; dimmed unopened files

production_viz.label: Empty — still generic
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring S06's layout: a PROJECT frame with a crimson X where the documents should be. An arrow labelled 'label changed, context didn't' points to an output box reading 'GENERIC' struck through in crimson-adjacent INK. A few dimmed, unopened file icons sit beside the frame, greyed out. Crimson X is the beat's accent.

beats.narration_text: A blank chat and an empty project behave the same way. Claude only sharpens once you feed it the documents you'd otherwise keep re-explaining.

props.quote: A blank chat and an empty project behave the same way. Claude only sharpens once you feed it the documents you'd otherwise keep re-explaining.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Here are the documents I keep re-explaining at work. Read them, then tell me what a new teammate still wouldn't understand — and what I should add to this project so I never have to explain it again. Paste that into a Claude project with your real files attached. Liam, in for Bear.
